title: The Salt Wreck
premise: Mirabel Iversen, captain of the riverboat Salt Wreck, is paid to deliver supplies to an archaeological expedition upriver — but when the camp goes silent and she finds it burned, she discovers the survivors are hiding from the very men who hired her: a smuggling ring using the dig as cover. With monsoon season closing in and her boat taking on water, Mirabel and the expedition's disgraced cartographer, Elio, must ferry the survivors downriver through flooded gorges while evading the smugglers' gunboat. The price of survival forces Mirabel to choose between her own debt and delivering justice the law can't reach, and in the end she scuttles the smugglers' boat at the Devil's Teeth rapids — losing her beloved Salt Wreck but gaining a crew of her own.
about_author: Beatrix Marchetti is a former river guide who spent six seasons working the waterways she now writes about, and her fiction is known for its tidal sense of pacing and unsentimental heart. She lives in a houseboat with two dogs and an unreliable shortwave radio.

chapters.title: Every Sandbar's Mood
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She pilots the Salt Wreck downriver, dodging a debt collector's summons and taking a lucrative contract to supply the Hollis expedition upriver. We learn her compass belonged to her dead father and her boat is all she has. Beat: weary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Contract
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In the port town of Vess, she negotiates with the smooth-talking Mr. Corvane, who overpays her and asks too many questions about the river above the falls. She loads supplies she doesn't recognize — crates heavier than they should be. Beat: unease beneath greed.

chapters.title: Upstream of Silence
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The ascent through the gorge, radio crackling with the expedition's last garbled transmission: 'not who we thought.' She anchors for the night as the first monsoon clouds stack on the horizon. Beat: dread arriving with the weather.

chapters.title: Ash on the Water
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She reaches the expedition camp and finds it burned, three days cold. One survivor — Elio Sarr, the cartographer — emerges from the mangroves with a rifle he doesn't know how to use and a waterproof case he refuses to surrender. Beat: suspicion between strangers.

chapters.title: What the Case Holds
chapters.summary: Elio's POV. He reveals the crates were smuggling contraband — black-market antiquities — and the expedition's leader discovered it. Corvane's men burned the camp and killed the professor. The case holds the professor's evidence ledger. Beat: the weight of proof and grief.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Corvane's enforcer, Dane Rook, catches up by launch and offers Mirabel triple her pay to hand over Elio and the case. She refuses — not from virtue, she insists, but spite — and they barely escape a shot across the bow. Beat: defiance born of anger, not nobility.

chapters.title: Leaking
chapters.summary: Elio's POV. The Salt Wreck's hull, strained by the gorge run, begins taking water. Elio, useless with engines, learns to bail and patch, and the two begin an uneasy partnership. He admits he took the expedition's money knowing what it carried. Beat: shared guilt as common ground.

chapters.title: The Widow of Kessel Bend
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. They stop at an isolated stilt-house where old Nesta Kessel trades fuel and rumors. Nesta recognizes the contraband's mark — the same men who burned her son's ferry years ago, a crime the river courts never punished. Beat: the theme of justice outside the law made flesh.

chapters.title: Monsoon
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The monsoon breaks with full fury. They shelter in a flooded limestone cave, and in the dark Mirabel tells Elio about her father — drowned running a debt he couldn't pay, compass recovered downstream. Beat: intimacy through shared shelter.

chapters.title: Rook's Bargain
chapters.summary: Elio's POV. Rook ambushes them at the cave mouth, but instead of shooting, he offers Elio a deal: the ledger for Elio's life, revealing that Corvane has a man inside the river authority — no legal report will ever land. Beat: hope of lawful justice dies.

chapters.title: The Devil's Teeth
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The only way past Rook's launch is the unrunnable rapids. Mirabel, who has never run them, studies her father's old notes all night. Elio maps the water from the cliff top, combining his charts with her instinct. Beat: terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Running the Teeth
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The run itself — a white-knuckle chapter through the rapids, hull screaming, Elio bailing for his life. They survive with the boat holed but afloat, and Rook's launch, following, wrecks on the outer teeth. Beat: triumph that costs something.

chapters.title: Strangers in the Reeds
chapters.summary: Elio's POV. They find two more expedition survivors — the professor's teenage daughter, Juno, and the wounded cook, Amara — hiding downstream. The Salt Wreck is now a lifeboat for four. Beat: found family assembling under duress.

chapters.title: Fever
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Amara's wound turns septic. Mirabel must choose: the long safe route to a doctor, or the short route past Corvane's checkpoint at the toll bridge. She chooses speed. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge
chapters.summary: Elio's POV. They bluff through the checkpoint with Juno — the professor's daughter, unknown to Corvane — posing as a merchant's child while Mirabel hides Amara below. Corvane himself inspects the boat and nearly finds the ledger. Beat: a held breath across ten pages.

chapters.title: Amara's Confession
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Recovering, she admits she helped load the contraband for money to pay her own family's debts — the same trap Mirabel's father died in. Mirabel, furious, then forgiving, sees her own history in it. Beat: the debt theme turned inward.

chapters.title: What Corvane Wants
chapters.summary: Elio's POV. Reading the ledger fully, they learn Corvane isn't just smuggling — he's buying the river itself, buying concessions and officials, and the professor's evidence is the only thing that can break his empire. Beat: the stakes widen from escape to war.

chapters.title: The Trap at Low Water
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Rook survived the wreck and Corvane has blockaded the last deep channel. Mirabel proposes the unthinkable: use the Salt Wreck as bait, lure the gunboat into the shallows she knows by heart, and take the fight to them. Beat: the hunted turning hunter.

chapters.title: Sandbar Justice
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The ambush — Mirabel runs the gunboat aground on a hidden bar, Elio and Amara board under cover of rain, and Rook, cornered, is given the choice the river gives everyone: swim or answer for the professor. Beat: justice outside the law, paid in full.

chapters.title: Scuttling
chapters.summary: Elio's POV. Corvane, desperate, rams the Salt Wreck rather than be taken alive. Mirabel gets everyone off, but the boat — her father's boat, her whole inheritance — goes down in the shallows. Beat: grief and release entangled; the price of survival.

chapters.title: The Ledger Lands
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Downriver at last, they deliver the ledger not to the compromised river authority but to Nesta Kessel's network of river families, who have waited years to testify. The monsoon breaks into sunlight. Beat: justice as something built by hands, not courts.

chapters.title: A New Hull
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, weeks later. The river families, grateful, help her raise the Salt Wreck's bones and rebuild — with Elio drafting the plans and Juno and Amara hammering alongside. Her father's compass still points true. She has a debt, a crew, and a home. Beat: found family as resolution.
